subject: ClearPath private deployment: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S — connectivity recommendation request
messages:
From: Jared Solano <jared@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearPath NetOps <netops@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity — quick info + constraints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call earlier. ClearPath is evaluating Redwood Private for a PHI-handling inference workload. NetOps asked me to capture a few constraints so your team can advise which connectivity pattern makes sense:

- High compliance bar (SOC2 + HIPAA).
- Prefer traffic never transits the public internet if possible.
- We run across multiple AWS accounts and two regions (us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 DR).
- Our current VPC CIDR ranges are overlapping across some dev accounts; production ranges are unique.
- Expected steady-state peak: ~600 requests/sec, typical payloads ~3KB, token sizes small, but we need <120ms p99 for inference calls.

Attaching a rough network diagram and the NetOps questionnaire (they filled some answers). Can you outline tradeoffs between VPC peering, PrivateLink, and site-to-site VPN for this profile and what you would recommend for an initial production rollout?

Appreciate a short recommendation and any caveats so we can bring this back to ClearPath NetOps.

Thanks,
Jared
Head of Integrations
ClearPath Health

[attachment: clearpath_netops_req.xlsx]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Solano <jared@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: ClearPath NetOps <netops@clearpathhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick info + constraints

Jared — thanks for the detail and the attachments. I pulled Marcus (serving infra) and Kimberly (eng manager) in for technical + rollout guidance. High level summary below, then a recommended phased approach.

Short summary of tradeoffs (one-liners):
- VPC peering: lowest network hop count and cost per byte, but not transitive and breaks if CIDR ranges overlap; best for same-account or coordinated CIDRs and when you need high throughput with minimal packet transformation.
- PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoints): avoids CIDR overlap and exposes a service endpoint in your VPC via ENIs; good for strict inbound control and cross-account access; incur per-ENI hourly and per-GB costs and additional connection management (endpoint services).
- Site-to-site VPN (S2S): easiest to stand up for initial proof-of-concept; encrypted over the public internet or via a transit provider, lower hourly infra cost but higher latency and jitter, and operational overhead for reliability at scale.

Recommended phased plan for ClearPath given your constraints and p99 target (~120ms):
1) Short POC: start S2S with BGP to validate functional integration and request volumes (2–4 weeks). Instrument token-level latency and error metrics.
2) Production: aim for PrivateLink if you require strict non-public routing and you have multiple AWS accounts with overlapping CIDRs — it maps cleanly to cross-account access without changing IP ranges.
3) If ClearPath can coordinate non-overlapping CIDRs across production VPCs (or use a transit VPC with NAT), VPC peering between the Redwood VPC and ClearPath prod VPC in us-east-1 gives the best per-request latency and lower data egress cost. For multi-region DR we recommend PrivateLink in the secondary region or setting up cross-region peering if available/acceptable.

Caveats:
- PrivateLink can add ~5–25ms depending on ENI placement and processing; VPC peering typically lowest.
- Throughput: if you expect bursts >1,000 r/s we’ll want to validate connection bandwidth and ensure we provision endpoints/ENIs accordingly.
- Failover: design an automated fallback (Private -> peered path or hosted API) in case endpoints saturate.

Next asks from our side:
- Confirm which accounts ClearPath wants Redwood to expose endpoints into (account IDs).
- Confirm production CIDRs (especially for prod VPCs).
- Any procurement/compliance tunneling constraints (e.g., requirement for on-prem NVA/IDS in path).

I attached an initial SOW draft and a diagram. Marcus — can you add two bullets on latency and expected throughput limitations for each pattern?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick info + constraints

Adding the technical delta as requested. I ran some internal perf numbers and reasoning for the three paths:

1) VPC Peering (same region)
- Latency: ~1–6ms median inside AWS AZ to AZ; p99 can be <10ms if same AZ, otherwise ~10–20ms cross-AZ.
- Throughput: essentially limited by instance ENI and NIC; multiple parallel TCP connections will saturate at several Gbps depending on instance type. No per-GB endpoint cost.
- Ops: need matching/unique CIDRs; not transitive — if ClearPath wants multiple peered VPCs we may need an explicit peering for each.

2) PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint to Redwood service)
- Latency: additional hop to service ENI; expect +8–25ms p50/p99 depending on placement and processing inside our infra.
- Throughput: per ENI limitations; you can scale by adding multiple endpoints and load distribution. There is an hourly endpoint cost + per-GB.
- Ops: handles cross-account and overlapping CIDR cases cleanly; supports strict ingress controls via SGs and endpoint policies.

3) Site-to-Site VPN (BGP/IPsec)
- Latency: depends on public internet path; expect +20–100ms and higher jitter. Not suitable if you need stable sub-120ms p99 consistently unless using dedicated private circuits (e.g., AWS Direct Connect or partner MPLS).
- Throughput: limited, and you must manage tunnel failover; AWS managed VPNs can throttle under load.
- Ops: lowest initial infra cost, but higher operational overhead and less deterministic SLA.

Operational recommendations:
- For prod with SOC2/HIPAA and sub-120ms p99: target VPC peering if you can guarantee non-overlapping prod CIDRs and want lowest latency. If cross-account CIDR conflict or you cannot change IPs, target PrivateLink and design for multiple endpoints to scale.
- Use S2S as POC or for regional DR if limited budget, but expect higher latencies and set realistic SLOs.
- Implement per-route and per-endpoint monitoring; expose token-level latency to ClearPath for immediate troubleshooting.

I can produce a short config checklist (SG rules, endpoint service creation, peering accept flow, BGP params) if you want.

—Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Jared Solano <jared@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick info + constraints

Quick decision guidance from a rollout/contract perspective:

- Procurement: PrivateLink plus endpoint-hours and per-GB billing needs to be explicitly captured in SOW if ClearPath chooses that path. We should include a clause for endpoint scaling and a monthly cap for the first 3 months.
- Compliance: we will sign BAAs and the required SOC2 evidence, but PrivateLink avoids the need to traverse public IP space which customers like ClearPath often prefer for PHI.
- Canary plan: agree POC over S2S for 2 weeks, then staged migration to PrivateLink in prod VPCs (or peering if they can standardize CIDRs). Staged traffic split: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2–3 weeks with rollback triggers on token error rate or latency regressions.

Soojin: create a proposed SOW addendum showing estimated monthly costs for PrivateLink (endpoints + egress) vs peering (egress only). Jared: once we get account IDs and prod CIDRs we can finalize.

Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
